scope: Local follow-up source candidate against the unchanged deployed 0.7.2 ARM64 relay; ten headless production-session clients on one Mac over Wi-Fi, no injected WAN impairment.

audit_driver_stall.finding: Full canonical snapshot comparisons blocked the thread pumping all ten clients. Delayed batches made the host consumer miss receive-queue drain opportunities.
audit_driver_stall.correction: Move the unchanged Agreement oracle to a bounded 512-sample worker queue. Fail on queue exhaustion, drain all submitted samples, and fail if any peer tick is missing. Gameplay transport buffers and acceptance thresholds are unchanged.

prediction_clock_rewind.finding: An input observed between fixed captures could rebuild the same canonical baseline after owner retention, reducing the predicted tick and replacing its position with the host forecast.
prediction_clock_rewind.correction: Retain validated owner motion on repeated rebuilds, and keep the active prediction target at least the previous predicted tick within the existing prediction bound.

stale_walking_pose.finding: Position equality was used as pose equality. A host forecast reaching the stopped owner position replaced its idle gait with walking.
stale_walking_pose.correction: Compare the full native AvatarMotion, including gait, when retaining owner motion. Shared collision validation remains active.

limitations: The published 0.7.2 clients still contain the prediction defects; these corrections are local source changes.
The production relay stayed on the published 0.7.2 executable; no production version A/B comparison was performed.
Headless state/render oracles do not measure physical display, input-device or audio latency.
Only one ten-client WAN room at a time was retested, not forty simultaneous WAN clients.
The original failures and the startup timeout are retained; three passing repetitions do not guarantee all future Internet conditions.
Raw report/log hashes refer to retained local build artifacts; the compact measurements and failure samples are embedded here.
